\chapter{Looking After Each Other}
\label{ch:ml-looking-after-each-other}
\hlchaptermodality{559}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can say to look after, to hold close, to get along, to cherish and to ask forgiveness.}

Complete the last lesson of chapter 559: I can say to look after, to hold close, to get along, to cherish and to ask forgiveness.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{പരിപാലിക്കുക} (paripālikkuka)}{പരിപാലിക്കുക (paripālikkuka)}]{\ml{പരിപാലിക്കുക} (paripālikkuka) — to look after; to maintain}

\label{lesson:ML-C559-paripalikkuka}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for grown-up, then the Malayalam for a twin.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{പരിപാലിക്കുക}}
\textbf{\ml{പരിപാലിക്കുക}} — \emph{paripālikkuka} — \textquotedblleft{}to look after; to maintain\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{വിരമിച്ച} \ml{ശേഷം} \ml{അച്ഛൻ} \ml{പൂന്തോട്ടം} \ml{പരിപാലിക്കുന്നു}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{viramicca śēṣaṁ acchan pūntōṭṭaṁ paripālikkunnu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Since retiring, Father has been looking after the garden.
\end{quote}

Past: \ml{പരിപാലിച്ചു}, \emph{paripāliccu}.

The noun is \ml{പരിപാലനം}, upkeep.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{പരിപാലിക്കുക}} (\emph{paripālikkuka}) is built from Sanskrit \emph{paripālana}, \textquotedblleft{}guarding, fostering\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams), with the Malayalam verb ending -\ml{ിക്കുക}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{paripālikkuka}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{paripālikkuka}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{viramicca śēṣaṁ acchan pūntōṭṭaṁ paripālikkunnu.} — Since retiring, Father has been looking after the garden.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for grown-up, then the Malayalam for a twin, then say \emph{paripālikkuka} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{പരിപാലിക്കുക} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To look after; to maintain\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{ചേർത്തുപിടിക്കുക} (cērttupiṭikkuka)}{ചേർത്തുപിടിക്കുക (cērttupiṭikkuka)}]{\ml{ചേർത്തുപിടിക്കുക} (cērttupiṭikkuka) — to hold close}

\label{lesson:ML-C559-certtupitikkuka}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for a twin, then the Malayalam for to look after.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{ചേർത്തുപിടിക്കുക}}
\textbf{\ml{ചേർത്തുപിടിക്കുക}} — \emph{cērttupiṭikkuka} — \textquotedblleft{}to hold close\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{കരയുന്ന} \ml{കുട്ടിയെ} \ml{അമ്മ} \ml{ചേർത്തുപിടിച്ചു}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{karayunna kuṭṭiye amma cērttupiṭiccu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Mother held the crying child close.
\end{quote}

Past: \ml{ചേർത്തുപിടിച്ചു}, \emph{cērttupiṭiccu}.

\ml{ചേർത്ത്}, having joined, + \ml{പിടിക്കുക}, to hold.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{ചേർത്തുപിടിക്കുക}} (\emph{cērttupiṭikkuka}) is native Dravidian, a compound of \ml{ചേർക്കുക}, \textquotedblleft{}to join, to bring close\textquotedblright{} (DEDR 2814), and \ml{പിടിക്കുക}, \textquotedblleft{}to seize, to hold\textquotedblright{} (DEDR 4148).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{cērttupiṭikkuka}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{cērttupiṭikkuka}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{karayunna kuṭṭiye amma cērttupiṭiccu.} — Mother held the crying child close.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for a twin, then the Malayalam for to look after, then say \emph{cērttupiṭikkuka} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{ചേർത്തുപിടിക്കുക} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To hold close\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{ഒത്തുപോകുക} (ottupōkuka)}{ഒത്തുപോകുക (ottupōkuka)}]{\ml{ഒത്തുപോകുക} (ottupōkuka) — to get along; to fit in}

\label{lesson:ML-C559-ottupokuka}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for to look after, then the Malayalam for to hold close.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{ഒത്തുപോകുക}}
\textbf{\ml{ഒത്തുപോകുക}} — \emph{ottupōkuka} — \textquotedblleft{}to get along; to fit in\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{പുതിയ} \ml{ഓഫീസിലെ} \ml{എല്ലാവരുമായി} \ml{അവൾ} \ml{നന്നായി} \ml{ഒത്തുപോകുന്നു}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{putiya ōphīsile ellāvarumāyi avaḷ nannāyi ottupōkunnu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
She gets along well with everyone at the new office.
\end{quote}

Past: \ml{ഒത്തുപോയി}, \emph{ottupōyi}.

The person takes -\ml{ഉമായി}, with: \ml{അവരുമായി} \ml{ഒത്തുപോകുക}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{ഒത്തുപോകുക}} (\emph{ottupōkuka}) is native Dravidian, a compound of \ml{ഒത്ത്}, from \ml{ഒക്കുക}, \textquotedblleft{}to agree, to be alike\textquotedblright{} (DEDR 924), and \ml{പോകുക}, \textquotedblleft{}to go\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ottupōkuka}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ottupōkuka}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{putiya ōphīsile ellāvarumāyi avaḷ nannāyi ottupōkunnu.} — She gets along well with everyone at the new office.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for to look after, then the Malayalam for to hold close, then say \emph{ottupōkuka} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{ഒത്തുപോകുക} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To get along; to fit in\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{കാത്തുസൂക്ഷിക്കുക} (kāttusūkṣikkuka)}{കാത്തുസൂക്ഷിക്കുക (kāttusūkṣikkuka)}]{\ml{കാത്തുസൂക്ഷിക്കുക} (kāttusūkṣikkuka) — to cherish; to safeguard}

\label{lesson:ML-C559-kattusuksikkuka}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for to hold close, then the Malayalam for to get along.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{കാത്തുസൂക്ഷിക്കുക}}
\textbf{\ml{കാത്തുസൂക്ഷിക്കുക}} — \emph{kāttusūkṣikkuka} — \textquotedblleft{}to cherish; to safeguard\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{മുത്തശ്ശി} \ml{പഴയ} \ml{ഫോട്ടോകൾ} \ml{കാത്തുസൂക്ഷിച്ചു}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{muttaśśi paḻaya phōṭṭōkaḷ kāttusūkṣiccu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Grandmother kept the old photos safe.
\end{quote}

Past: \ml{കാത്തുസൂക്ഷിച്ചു}, \emph{kāttusūkṣiccu}.

\ml{കാത്ത്} guarding + \ml{സൂക്ഷിക്കുക} to keep with care; \ml{സൂക്ഷിക്കണേ}, take care, holds the second part.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{കാത്തുസൂക്ഷിക്കുക}} (\emph{kāttusūkṣikkuka}) is a Malayalam compound built from \ml{കാത്ത്}, from the native verb \ml{കാക്കുക}, \textquotedblleft{}to keep, to guard\textquotedblright{} (DEDR 1416), and \ml{സൂക്ഷിക്കുക}, from Sanskrit \emph{sūkṣma}, \textquotedblleft{}fine, minute\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 13546).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kāttusūkṣikkuka}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kāttusūkṣikkuka}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{muttaśśi paḻaya phōṭṭōkaḷ kāttusūkṣiccu.} — Grandmother kept the old photos safe.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for to hold close, then the Malayalam for to get along, then say \emph{kāttusūkṣikkuka} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{കാത്തുസൂക്ഷിക്കുക} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To cherish; to safeguard\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{ക്ഷമ} \ml{ചോദിക്കുക} (kṣama cōdikkuka)}{ക്ഷമ ചോദിക്കുക (kṣama cōdikkuka)}]{\ml{ക്ഷമ} \ml{ചോദിക്കുക} (kṣama cōdikkuka) — to ask forgiveness; to apologise}

\label{lesson:ML-C559-ksama-codikkuka}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for to get along, then the Malayalam for to cherish.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{ക്ഷമ} \ml{ചോദിക്കുക}}
\textbf{\ml{ക്ഷമ} \ml{ചോദിക്കുക}} — \emph{kṣama cōdikkuka} — \textquotedblleft{}to ask forgiveness; to apologise\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{വൈകി} \ml{വന്നതിന്} \ml{അവൻ} \ml{അധ്യാപകനോട്} \ml{ക്ഷമ} \ml{ചോദിച്ചു}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{vaiki vannatinŭ avan adhyāpakanōṭŭ kṣama cōdiccu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
He apologised to the teacher for coming late.
\end{quote}

Past: \ml{ക്ഷമ} \ml{ചോദിച്ചു}, \emph{kṣama cōdiccu}.

What one apologises for takes -\ml{ഇന്}, the person -\ml{ഓട്}. \ml{മാപ്പ്} \ml{ചോദിക്കുക} says the same.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{ക്ഷമ} \ml{ചോദിക്കുക}} (\emph{kṣama cōdikkuka}) is a Malayalam phrase built from \ml{ക്ഷമ}, from Sanskrit \emph{kṣamā}, \textquotedblleft{}patience, forbearance\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 3659), and \ml{ചോദിക്കുക}, \textquotedblleft{}to ask\textquotedblright{}: to ask for forbearance.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kṣama cōdikkuka}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{vaiki vannatinŭ avan adhyāpakanōṭŭ kṣama cōdiccu.} — He apologised to the teacher for coming late.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for to get along, then the Malayalam for to cherish, then say \emph{kṣama cōdikkuka} again
\end{itemize}
